failures.resolution: First live turn against the freshly created coach-eval branch; fast path returned the correct action (remove_from_avoid) but took 2008 ms against the 2000 ms bound, an 8 ms (0.4%) overshoot consistent with a cold Postgres/pooler connection on a brand-new branch rather than a sustained regression.

openHarness only set COACH_ACTIVITY_CONTEXT_ENABLED when --category activity was passed explicitly, so the default (category === null) run drew the corpus's one activity case without the flag: no activity block in context, the coach fell back from gemini-3.6-flash to gemini-3.8-flash on capacity after 8975 ms, then timed out at 30675 ms against the 15000 ms bound, producing the generic retry line instead of the expected device-estimate copy. Fixed by extracting needsActivityContext(category) (true for 'activity' and for the default null run) and using it at the openHarness call site in runStreak.

Gemini hit a capacity limit on gemini-3.6-flash and fell back to gemini-3.8-flash after 4002 ms; the fallback call then ran long and tripped the harness's own 30 s total-budget abort (deadline copy: 'That took too long and I stopped. Ask me again.'), producing 0 cards against the expected 1-3 and a 30437 ms elapsed time against the 15000 ms bound. Provider-side capacity/latency, not a code or corpus defect.

Gemini returned 503 'currently experiencing high demand' on both gemini-3.6-flash and its gemini-3.8-flash capacity fallback; the coach turn surfaced the honest 'Sasha is unavailable right now' error. Live provider outage, not a code or corpus defect.

Gemini capacity fallback (gemini-3.6-flash -> gemini-3.8-flash) then the fallback call ran past the 30 s harness budget, returning 0 cards/no anchors against the expected 5 distinct protein-anchor cards. Same ongoing live-provider capacity event as F003/F004, not a code or corpus defect.

The food_search tool call's intent argument is model-chosen (lib/coach/blocks/hydrate-food-search.ts maps the model's own 'browse'/'eats'/'avoid'/'lookup' tool argument to a persisted intent; there is no deterministic classifier here). For 'show me watermelon in the catalog so I can decide whether to avoid it' the model called the tool with intent=browse (persisted as log) instead of avoid, despite the user's explicit avoid-leaning phrasing. Everything else about the turn was correct (reply, block kind, card count, latency, no unsupported claim). A model intent-selection miss, not a code or corpus defect -- the corpus's expected 'avoid' matches the user's stated intent.

seedRehearsal never persisted a target_profiles revision, only user_settings. Post target-authority-boundary (docs/decisions/2026-09-22-target-priors.md), compose_meal/suggest_options never invent numbers from user_settings alone -- without an effective target_profiles row the coach answered 'Your targets aren't set yet. Finish your profile and I'll size options to your target.' on the fast path (1516 ms, no model/latency issue) instead of composing any card. This deterministically breaks every corpus case expecting a sized suggestion (suggest-three-dinners and 7 others: devin-five-eats-suggestions, devin-remaining-snack, suggest-chicken-wrap-wish, suggest-small-snack-wish, suggest-no-cook-recipes-wish, block-three-dinner-ideas, jev-three-dinner-ideas -- several of those also failed on this run but were attributed to the concurrent Gemini capacity outage since they timed out before reaching this gate). Fixed by calling the app's own write_target_revision RPC (same one tests/coach/suggest-new-account.test.ts uses) in seedRehearsal with a fixture consistent with the seeded user_settings.

blockers.resolution: Jev facet cache (food_facets.contains_soy) was never warmed on the brand-new coach-eval branch. Ran the documented warm workflow: coach-streak.ts --category jev --prepare-jev to get the plan ({userId, catalogAfter:0, limit:18}), then scripts/warm-facets.ts --commit --user-id <id> --limit 18 against the branch (450 judged, 0 errors). catalog_revision:11 (Smoked tofu) now has contains_soy p=0.98, above the present threshold. One-time per-branch setup, not a code or corpus defect; resuming.
